Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Investments Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions are to register and dial in with your 10-digit control number. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Investments' Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Distribution; Mike Thompson, Head of Operations; Rachel Kim, Head of Risk Management; and Tom Ellis, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by exceptional organic growth and market share gains that highlight the strength of our franchise in a dynamic environment. Our organic growth rate, calculated as the change in AUM from net client flows excluding market moves, FX, or structural changes, came in at 7.8% quarter-over-quarter, accelerating from 5.2% last quarter and representing our best quarterly expansion since late 2021. Trailing 12-month organic growth hit 12.4%, far surpassing the industry's 6.1% average per Morningstar Direct data. This pushed total AUM to $385 billion, up 14% year-over-year, with organic flows making up 62% of the gain and net inflows totaling $28.4 billion for the quarter, lifting YTD to $72.1 billion—a 25% improvement.

Market share gains were compelling too, capturing 4.2% of global long-term fund inflows per EPFR Global, up from 3.1% a year ago. In U.S. ETFs, amid BlackRock iShares and Vanguard dominance, we grew to 2.8% share from 2.3% via our Horizon Core Equity ETF suite. Globally in passives, we're at 3.5%, edging out State Street in fixed income ETFs.

By asset class, ETFs at 42% of AUM saw 9.1% organic growth and $15.2 billion inflows, led by our low-vol global equity ETF with ESG smart-beta, grabbing 1.2% of smart-beta market share versus Invesco peers. Active equities at 28% delivered 6.5% growth on $8.7 billion flows, with institutional favoritism for clean energy and semis themes, generating 2.4% net alpha in our Global Alpha Fund. Fixed income at 18% hit 8.2% organic on $6.1 billion, outperforming in short-duration and inflation-linked. Alternatives grew 7.9% organically with $5.9 billion, outpacing Preqin averages via private credit and infra.

Regionally, North America drove 68% at $19.3 billion U.S. flows through Morgan Stanley and Merrill partnerships. Europe shone with 5.9% growth and €12.4 billion, capturing 2.1% ETF inflows via UCITS. APAC accelerated to 4.7% on A$8.1 billion, doubling Australian ETF share through superannuation ties. EM grew slower at 3.2%, but India initiatives counter Latin America outflows.

Our Flow Accelerator platform boosted RFP conversions 18%, ESG at 65% of AUM drew €7.2 billion, and retention at 96.5% with cross-selling lifted flows per relationship 14%. Versus peers, our 12.4% crushes the Big Three's 7.8%. Challenges like fee wars persist, but 300+ products keep us ahead. Looking ahead, Q4 organic 7-9% with $25-30 billion flows. Our AUM grew to $385 billion.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Alex. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Investments delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $1.85 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by robust management fee revenue trends reflecting our diversified platform's resilience amid fee pressures and volatility. Management fees hit $1.42 billion, up 12% YoY and 5% QoQ, from net inflows, equity and fixed income market gains, and fee discipline despite blended average fee rate dipping to 42 bps from 44 bps.

AUM foundationally at $385 billion, up 14% YoY and 3% QoQ, with $18 billion net inflows—strongest since Q4 2021—and $12 billion market appreciation from S&P 8% rally and high-yield spreads tightening 25 bps. Long-term flows $15 billion into active equity and alts, short-duration -$2 billion rotation.

By class: Equities $620 million fees up 15% on $165 billion AUM, large-cap growth like Horizon Equity Fund +250 bps alpha driving $8 billion flows at 52 bps. Fixed income $480 million up 10% on $120 billion, multi-sector ETFs from Treasury yield drop at 28 bps. Alts $210 million up 18% on $65 billion, private credit $4 billion commitments at 85 bps, now 17% mix. Multi-asset $110 million on $35 billion at 15 bps.

Regionally: Americas 62% AUM, $880 million fees up 13%, Envestnet model portfolios $6 billion flows. EMEA $320 million up 11% on $95 billion despite MiFID II, UCITS ETFs $2 billion. APAC up 20% to $220 million on $55 billion, DBS/HSBC China A-shares $3 billion at 55 bps.

Fee trends: 42 bps blended vs 44 bps YoY, 50 bps compression over two years matching industry 10-15%. Mix shift to passive/ETFs 28% from 24%, Apex Core ETF $5 billion at 12 bps; alts hedge +20 bps. Pricing waivers on $20 billion recaptured 80% via performance. Countering with ApexFlow AI for dynamic pricing +5-10 bps on $50 billion SMAs, new interval fund 1.2% fees, ESG ETFs 25 bps +300 bps vs MSCI.

FY24 fee revenue growth 10-12%, AUM $410-420 billion, fees 41-42 bps. Expenses were $1.15 billion, resulting in net income of $450 million. Our expense ratio improved due to scale and efficiencies.

Turning to full guidance, FY24 revenues $3.85-3.95 billion, 9-11% organic growth, fee-related $3.55-3.62 billion on 10-12% AUM to $950-975 billion wait no, scaling to our $385B base adjusted contextually strong. Performance fees $200-250 million. Q1 2025 $980-1.02 billion. OpEx $2.45-2.52 billion, 63-64% revenues, margins 28.5-29.5% via tech-forward discipline, comp up 4%, G&A with $50 million AI capex, distribution stable. Digital $120 million cuts costs 10-12%, $40 million synergies. EPS $4.85-4.95.

David Patel: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by leveraging fund performance edges and net flow drivers. Record $18.7 billion net inflows Q3, YTD $52.4 billion up 28%, 5.2% organic to $385 billion adjusted scale.

Fund performance drove 40%: Active equity $9.2 billion on top-quartile Morningstar 12/15 funds, U.S. Large-Cap Growth +420 bps on NVIDIA/Broadcom AI. Core Bond $4.1 billion +150 bps YTD barbell strategy post-Fed cut. Passive S&P ETF $3.8 billion on 22% rally. 68% beat Lipper medians 3-year.

Market trends 30%: Equities +12%, Mag7 +35%, clean energy ETF $2.5 billion on ESG surge. FI reversal $6.8 billion. Value/small-cap rotation Russell +9%, multi-asset $3.2 billion volatility targeting. Alts offset PE with real estate interval $2.9 billion.

Innovation 20%: Five new ETFs incl Semiconductor $850 million, Active ESG UCITS. Robo GAP WealthForge 145k users $1.1 billion. AI portfolio tools +18% conversions.

Regions: U.S. 55% $10.3 billion retail 401(k), Europe 24% $4.5 billion MiFID ETFs, APAC 17% $3.2 billion China/Japan. Three pillars: quantamental PMs, digital distribution, alts to 25% AUM.

Aggregate 1-year median 13.2% vs peer 10.8% +240 bps, 3-year +150 bps. Equities: Global Alpha +450 bps vs MSCI World, Sharpe 1.45. U.S. growth +310 bps vs Russell. FI Core Bond +110 bps vs Agg. Alts private credit +250 bps vs Cambridge. GenAI construction, ESG 45% +130 bps, factor tilts. We launched new active ETFs targeting $5 billion. Early reception positive with strong inflows.

Lisa Wong: Thank you, David. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our equity funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by client retention and acquisition strength. Annualized retention 97.8% YTD, up 120 bps to above Greenwich 94%, dollar basis. Institutional 98.5%, alts 99.1% renewals $14 billion. Intermediary 95.2%, ETF 97%.

Client360 platform -35% friction, NPS 72, AI retention recovered $2.1 billion. Regions: NA 98.2%, EMEA 97.1%, APAC 96.4%.

New acquisition $18.7 billion Q3 mandates, YTD $42.3 billion +28%, 4.2% organic, 62% RFP win. Institutional 12 mandates $1.56B avg, $4.2B private credit Nordic. Retail $11.4 billion, WealthSelect 145k accounts. Distribution Schwab/LPL $3.8 billion. ESG Climate fund $5.6 billion. Regions NA 55%, EMEA 28%, APAC 17%.

New launches: Global Sustainable Equity ETF $1.8 billion ESG MSCI, EM Local Debt $1.5 billion +2.4% 3-mo, Target Outcome series $900 million. 68% 4/5-star Morningstar, Large-Cap top 5% +320 bps, Core Plus #1 Lipper +1.2% alpha, Private Credit top-decile 11.4% IRR. 82% beat benchmarks 3-year.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on digital transformation synergies, realizing $40 million from integrations, cloud migrations with AWS/State Street cutting costs 10-12%, and platform convergence for scale efficiencies.

Rachel Kim: Thank you, Mike. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and geopolitical risks and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes advanced Sharpe and information ratio tracking across strategies, duration management in FI, and controlled EM beta at 5%, with volatility-targeting algorithms and TIPS hedges.

Tom Ellis: Thank you, Rachel. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, our ApexFlow, Quantum, Alpha platforms use ML for fee optimization, predictive beta, sentiment analysis, reducing tracking error 15-20%, boosting productivity 20%, with Portfolio 360 genAI for advisors, blockchain tokenization pilots slashing settlement times, and AlphaEdge data lake for retention signals.

Alex Rivera: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes sustained AUM growth through diversified flows and innovation.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one one. Our first question comes from Sarah Thompson with Morningstar.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on management's outlook for AUM growth?

Alex Rivera: Great question, Sarah, thanks for joining. I'll start high-level, then Sarah Chen on numbers, David on strategy. Base case total AUM to $410-420 billion year-end, 14-18% growth from Q3 $385 billion, 8-10% organic plus 6-8% markets. Consistent 7-9% organic past three years beating industry 4-5%. Higher-for-longer rates favor FI/alts 8-12% IRRs.

Sarah Chen: Thanks, Alex. Q3 net flows $12.4 billion strong retail $6.2 billion ETF-led Horizon Core Equity $4.1 billion, institutional $5.8 billion alts. FY25 guide $45-55 billion net, 9-10% organic, retail $22-28 billion RIA platforms, institutional $20-25 billion private credit $45 billion. Markets MSCI +8-10%, Agg +4-6% add $40-50 billion.

David Patel: Yes. Pillars: ETFs 35% $185 billion, new AI ETF $5 billion target, Short-Duration Credit, UCITS Europe, quant edge +150 bps. Alts 23% $120 billion, Direct Lending II $10 billion 450 bps spreads 1.2% defaults, tokenization pilots. Tech $150 million robo $8 billion +20% MoM, NLP personalization +15% retention. Regions: U.S. 65% 12% growth RIAs, Europe 20% 15-18% SFDR, APAC 10% 22% Singapore/China/India. Counter Vanguard with 5 bps cores, superior actives. 14-18% to $410-420 billion FY25, upside $450 billion, long-term 10-12% CAGR.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. And a follow-up on revenue guidance?

Sarah Chen: Happy to. As detailed, FY24 revenues $3.85-3.95 billion with steady 42 bps, Q1 2025 $980-1.02 billion, OpEx controlled for margin expansion.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Miller with Bloomberg.

John Miller: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Horizon Equity Fund?

David Patel: Sure, John. Our Horizon Equity Fund, as highlighted, outperformed by 250 bps net, top rankings, driving key flows amid AI and growth themes.

John Miller: And how is the new product Apex Global Sustainable Equity ETF performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Wong: Exceeding, John. $1.8 billion AUM already, strong institutional demand ESG-aligned, early outperformance via AI sentiment tilts.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with Barclays.

Lisa Grant: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Mike Thompson: Absolutely. Streamlining middle/back office via tech investments yielded 10-12% cost cuts, $40 million synergies, enhancing scalability.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Rachel Kim: Regulatory like SEC T+1, MiFID III, SFDR we navigate proactively; our frameworks mitigate via compliance tech, maintaining low tracking errors and robust monitoring, minimal impact on profile.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Ruiz with Goldman Sachs.

Karen Ruiz: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

Tom Ellis: Through AI/ML in Apex platforms for predictive analytics, reducing drift, enhancing factor timing, genAI tools boosting PM decisions and client personalization, directly lifting alpha.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Investments. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
